Records|Warner Bros.]] | writer = Gary Wright | producer = Gary Wright | prev_title = [[Dream Weaver]] | prev_year = 1975 | next_title = Made to Love You | next_year = 1976 }} "'''Love Is Alive'''" is a song by [[Gary Wright]] taken from the 1975 album ''[[The Dream Weaver]]''. It features Wright on vocals and keyboards and [[Andy Newmark]] on drums, with all music except for the drums produced on the keyboards. The album's [[Dream Weaver|title cut]] and "Love Is Alive" both peaked at No. 2 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] singles chart. "Love Is Alive" spent 27 weeks on the chart, seven weeks longer than "Dream Weaver". ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' ranked "Love Is Alive" as the [[Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 1976|No. 9 song of 1976]]. In the US, "Love Is Alive" peaked at number two on the Hot 100, tied with "[[Dream Weaver]]" as his highest chart-topping single on that chart.[Joel Whitburn's Bubbling Under the Billboard Hot 100 1959-2004] "[[Kiss and Say Goodbye]]" by [[The Manhattans]] and "[[Don't Go Breaking My Heart]]" by [[Elton John]] and [[Kiki Dee]] kept it from the number one spot.[https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/1976-07-31 Hot 100: Week of July 31, 1976] billboard.com In Canada, the song reached No. 6.{{cite web|url=https://recherche-collection-search.bac-lac.gc.ca/eng/home/record?IdNumber=2611&app=rpm |title=Image : RPM Weekly - Library and Archives Canada |website=Bac-lac.gc.ca |date= 17 July 2013|access-date=2016-10-11}}

It features Wright on vocals and keyboards and Andy Newmark on drums, with all music except for the drums produced on the keyboards. The album's title cut and "Love Is Alive" both peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 singles chart. "Love Is Alive" spent 27 weeks on the chart, seven weeks longer than "Dream Weaver". Billboard ranked "Love Is Alive" as the No. 9 song of 1976. In the US, "Love Is Alive" peaked at number two on the Hot 100, tied with "Dream Weaver" as his highest chart-topping single on that chart. sections.heading: Covers and samples
sections.wikitext:
*[[Olivia Newton-John]] covered the track on her first live album ''[[Love Performance]]'' in 1976. She performed the song on her first 1976 [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC-TV]] special ''A Special Olivia Newton-John''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.needsomefun.net/november17-1976-olivia-newton-johns-first-tv-special-titled-a-very-special-olivia-newton-john-was-broadcast-on-abc-tv/|title=November 17, 1976 – Olivia Newton-John's first TV special titled "A Very Special Olivia Newton-John" was broadcast on ABC-TV |website=needsomefun.net |date=2020-11-22 |accessdate=2021-08-31}}</ref> and on a 1977 [[BBC]] special ''Only Olivia''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://70s-tv.com/only-olivia-1977-bbc-special/|title=Only Olivia 1977 BBC Special |website=70s-tv.com |date=1977-09-23 |accessdate=2021-08-31}}</ref>  Her rendition was also included as a bonus track on the 2010 Japanese re-issue of her 1978 album ''[[Totally Hot]]''.
*[[Chaka Khan]] covered the track as "My Love Is Alive" on her 1984 album ''[[I Feel for You (album)|I Feel For You]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/i-feel-for-you-mw0000650354  |title=I Feel For You by Alex Henderson |last=Henderson |first=Alex |work=[[allmusic]]}}</ref>
*In 1991, [[Joe Cocker]] covered "Love Is Alive" on his ''[[Night Calls (album)|Night Calls]]'' LP.  Released as a single, it reached number 72 in Canada and number 7 on the U.S. [[Mainstream Rock (chart)|Mainstream Rock]] chart in the summer of 1992.
*In 1997, [[Dance music|dance]] act [[3rd Party]] recorded the song for their debut album ''[[Alive (3rd Party album)|Alive]]'' which charted on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100. This version peaked at number 19 on the US ''Billboard'' [[Dance Club Songs|Hot Dance Music]] chart.<ref>{{cite book |title= Hot Dance/Disco: 1974-2003|last=Whitburn |first=Joel |author-link=Joel Whitburn |year=2004 |publisher=Record Research |page=257}}</ref>
*[[Joan Osborne]] covered the song on her album ''[[Righteous Love]]'' (2000). She frequently played it in concert, and one of these performances was included on the compilation album ''[[Radio Waves (Joan Osborne album)|Radio Waves]]'' (2022). The [[Associated Press]] called her cover version "improbably funky".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://toronto.citynews.ca/2022/02/23/review-joan-osborne-digs-into-her-archives-on-radio-waves/ |title=Review: Joan Osborne digs into her archives on 'Radio Waves' |last=Wine |first=Steven |date=February 26, 2022 |work=[[CityNews]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=February 16, 2024}}</ref>
*[[Anastacia]] covered the song on her 2000 debut album ''[[Not That Kind]]''. In 2001, it was re-recorded as a duet with [[Vonda Shepard]] for the TV show ''[[Ally McBeal]]''. It later appeared on the show's soundtrack album ''Ally McBeal: For Once in My Life''.
sections.text:
*Olivia Newton-John covered the track on her first live album Love Performance in 1976. She performed the song on her first 1976 ABC-TV special A Special Olivia Newton-John and on a 1977 BBC special Only Olivia.  Her rendition was also included as a bonus track on the 2010 Japanese re-issue of her 1978 album Totally Hot.
*Chaka Khan covered the track as "My Love Is Alive" on her 1984 album I Feel For You.
*In 1991, Joe Cocker covered "Love Is Alive" on his Night Calls LP.  Released as a single, it reached number 72 in Canada and number 7 on the U.S. Mainstream Rock chart in the summer of 1992.
*In 1997, dance act 3rd Party recorded the song for their debut album Alive which charted on the Billboard Hot 100. This version peaked at number 19 on the US Billboard Hot Dance Music chart.
*Joan Osborne covered the song on her album Righteous Love (2000). She frequently played it in concert, and one of these performances was included on the compilation album Radio Waves (2022). The Associated Press called her cover version "improbably funky".
*Anastacia covered the song on her 2000 debut album Not That Kind. In 2001, it was re-recorded as a duet with Vonda Shepard for the TV show Ally McBeal. It later appeared on the show's soundtrack album Ally McBeal: For Once in My Life.
